title: State Representation Shapes Long-Horizon Agent Learning and Transfer: An Empirical Study
abstract: arXiv:2610.15407v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An end-to-end success rate alone cannot distinguish failure to learn an action from failure to apply it as task state changes. We study this distinction in deterministic tool workflows that provide the current artifact state and candidate action recipes. Using 1.7B, 8B, and 27B Qwen models, we compare supervised learning across workflow horizons and cross the state representation used for training with the one used at evaluation. Horizon-matched supervision yields high completion, but an H4-trained 1.7B model transfers poorly to longer workflows under full-state observations. In an H16 crossover, compact-trained 1.7B adapters complete 50/50 held-out tasks in compact view and 0/50 in full view for each of three paired training seeds; full-trained outcomes vary across seeds. A separate 8B adapter pair shows a similar asymmetry. The view dependence also appears in paired-choice tasks where both candidate calls are executable and the correct

translated_title: 状态表示塑造长时程智能体学习与迁移：一项实证研究
translated_abstract: 仅凭端到端成功率无法区分“未能学会某个动作”与“随着任务状态变化而未能应用该动作”。我们在确定性工具工作流中研究这一区别，这些工作流会提供当前制品状态和候选动作配方。使用1.7B、8B和27B的Qwen模型，我们比较了不同工作流时程下的监督学习，并将训练时使用的状态表示与评估时使用的状态表示进行交叉对照。时程匹配的监督训练能带来较高的完成率，但在全状态观测下，H4训练的1.7B模型向更长工作流的迁移表现很差。在H16交叉实验中，用紧凑视图训练的1.7B适配器在三个配对训练种子中的每一个上，均在紧凑视图下完成50/50的保留任务，而在全视图下完成0/50；全视图训练的结果则因种子不同而变化。另一组独立的8B适配器对也显示出类似的不对称性。这种视图依赖性同样出现在配对选择任务中，即两个候选调用都可行且正确……
tldr: 该实证研究发现，状态表示的选择（紧凑视图 vs. 全视图）决定性地影响长时程智能体的学习与迁移能力——用紧凑状态表示训练的模型在全状态观测下完全无法应用所学动作，表明训练与评估间状态表示的不匹配是智能体迁移失败的关键原因。
en_tdlr: This empirical study shows that the choice of state representation (compact vs. full view) critically shapes long-horizon agent learning and transfer—adapters trained with compact state representations achieve 50/50 on held-out tasks under compact views but 0/50 under full-state observations, revealing that state representation mismatch between training and evaluation is a key cause of agent transfer failure.
